acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

params.implementation_: Deployed `IndexToken` bytecode that new clones point to.
params.initialOwner: Address that receives the owner role.

createIndex((address[],uint16[],address[.details: `nonReentrant` guards against a malicious implementation (set by a      compromised owner) re-entering `createIndex` from within the      `initialize` callback. Registry writes additionally happen      BEFORE the external `initialize` call (CEI ordering): if the      external call reverts, the storage writes revert atomically with      it, so a failed creation never leaves stale registry entries.

intentQueue().details: Returns the queue address that NEW clones will be initialized      with. Existing clones cache their queue at creation time and      are not affected by subsequent calls to `setIntentQueue` —      to find a specific clone's queue, call      `IndexToken(clone).intentQueue()` (or read the `IndexCreated`      event's last field).

minMint(address).details: Returns 0 if the admin has not set a value; in that case, mints in      that funding token revert with `IndexToken_AmountBelowMinimum`      (since `0` is also a hard floor caught earlier).

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setFeeHook(address).details: Discovery-only pointer per §17. Setting this does NOT retroactively      bind existing pools to the hook — V4 pools are bound to a hook      via the PoolKey at pool initialization. This setter exists so      the canonical hook for the protocol can be queried by frontends      and indexers without per-integration coordination. Zero is a      valid value (meaning "no canonical hook published yet").

setImplementation(address).details: Only affects future clones. Existing portfolios keep their original      implementation via ERC-1167's immutable-bytecode model. Rejects      addresses with no deployed code to prevent silently bricking      future creates with a typo'd / EOA address.

setIntentQueue(address).details: Zero is a valid value: it disables future async-containing baskets      while preserving sync-only flow. For non-zero values, the queue      is probed for `factory()` and must report this factory's address —      prevents accidentally binding new clones to a queue that doesn't      accept calls from this factory's clones (would silently break      every async basket created against the misconfigured queue).

setMinMint(address,uint256).details: Rejects `amount == 0` to prevent accidental floor removal. Setting      a tiny non-zero floor (e.g., 1 wei) is the explicit way to      effectively disable per-token gating.

setUnderlyingAllowed(address,bool).details: On the `allowed = true` path we probe ERC165 for the ERC777      and ERC1363 interface ids. Tokens that explicitly advertise      either are rejected — their transfer-time callbacks would      open read-only-reentrancy windows in `IndexToken.burn`,      `burnAsync` (Phase 2), and `cancelMint`. Non-ERC165 tokens      (most legacy ERC20s, including USDT/USDC/DAI) accept the      probe via the `try`/`catch` and pass through.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

createIndex((address[],uint16[],address[.notice: Deploys a new `IndexToken` clone configured as `cfg`.

feeHook().notice: The canonical {IXindexFeeHook} address (or zero if not yet set).

intentQueue().notice: The {IIntentQueue} address baked into every async-containing         clone at init time. May be `address(0)` until the admin         configures it; at that point only sync-only baskets can be         created.

isIndexToken(address).notice: True iff `account` is an `IndexToken` clone deployed by this         factory. Used by Phase 2 contracts (`IntentQueue`) to gate         calls that may only originate from registered index tokens.

minMint(address).notice: Per-funding-token minimum mint amount in native units.

setFeeHook(address).notice: Sets the canonical {IXindexFeeHook} pointer for off-chain         discovery. Setting this does NOT bind existing pools to the         hook (V4 pools are bound via PoolKey at init); it merely         publishes the canonical hook address so frontends and         indexers can locate it. Zero is a valid value.

setIntentQueue(address).notice: Sets the {IIntentQueue} address every async-containing         basket must point to. Setting to `address(0)` blocks future         async-containing baskets but does not affect already         deployed clones (they cache the queue at init).

setMinMint(address,uint256).notice: Sets the minimum mint amount (in `fundingToken` native units) that         every `IndexToken.mint` call denominated in `fundingToken` must         supply. Same floor applies to first and subsequent mints.

@title IndexFactory
 @notice Deploys and tracks `IndexToken` clones, enforces protocol allowlists.
 @dev Three allowlists gate what can appear in a new portfolio:
        - `isUnderlyingAllowed`: tokens usable as basket slots
        - `isFundingAllowed`: tokens users can pay with at mint time
        - `isAdapterAllowed`: adapters that can be referenced by baskets
      All three are admin-controlled via `Ownable2Step`. The factory owner
      also controls which implementation bytecode new clones point at; this
      never affects existing clones, because ERC-1167 minimal proxies bake
      the implementation address into immutable bytecode at deploy time.
      Security notes:
        - `Ownable2Step` is used instead of plain `Ownable` so that
          ownership transfer requires both a propose and an accept step.
          Prevents accidental transfer to an incorrect / inaccessible address.
        - Implementation swap affects ONLY future clones. Existing portfolio
          clones keep pointing at the implementation that was current when
          they were deployed — a critical property for users who rely on
          the immutability of their basket's logic.
        - Allowlist revocation affects future mints via the factory lookup
          in `IndexToken.mint`. This is an intentional global kill-switch
          for compromised funding tokens; existing holders can still burn
          because `burn` performs no factory lookup.
